content.text: A comprehensive mutual insurance regime exists in Section 12.3.

input.quote: 12.3.1 Generally. Commencing as of the Effective Date and thereafter during the Development Term, and subject to Section 12.3.2 below, each Party will carry and maintain, at its own expense, insurance coverage of the kind and with liability limits that, at a minimum, satisfy the requirements of Section 12.3.2, to protect itself and the other Party against any claims or liabilities that may arise from the conduct of the Clinical Trials and all other rights and obligations hereunder with insurers with a minimum "A-" A.M. Best rating.
input.rationale: Section 12.3 contains a full, mutual insurance regime that binds SFJ as well as PB, so the rule's concern (counterparty carrying cover) is satisfied. It requires A- rated insurers, commercial general liability (12.3.2.1), umbrella excess (12.3.2.2), clinical trials liability (12.3.2.3), professional liability for subcontractors providing professional services (12.3.2.4) with tail coverage, product liability with the other Party as additional insured (12.3.4), additional-insured status on clinical trial liability (12.3.3), certificates of insurance on written request annually (12.3.1), notice of cancellation or material change, and a requirement that each Party ensure its subcontractors (including Permitted Third Parties) are insured (12.3.1/12.3.2 flow-down). Section 12.3.2 also sets the floor at the greater of the stated limits or the highest limit required by Applicable Law. This meets or exceeds the preferred position on coverage types, tail, and certificates. Two points noted but not flagged: the dollar limits are redacted ([***]) in this filed copy so we cannot confirm they reach USD 1M/2M CGL and USD 2M E&O, and there is no express cyber/privacy liability line despite the personally identifiable information provisions in Article 11 — a missing sub-element rather than a fallback failure, given SFJ is a co-development funder rather than a hosting vendor processing our data. We would confirm limits against the unredacted schedule in diligence.
